claim.why_it_matters: The column structure of Figure D.6 is lost: form-zone labels are fused with PAGE clause phrase names ("Logical Top Heading", "Logical Page Limit"), "of Form" lands in the phrase column of a partial two-column table, and the rest of the figure is free text, so the association of each PAGE clause phrase with its form position and report content is garbled. verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 880 (printed 856) shows Figure D.6 as three columns: an italic, unheaded form-zone column (Physical Top of Form, Logical Top of Form, Logical Bottom of Form, Physical Bottom of Form) left of a vertical rule, a bold PAGE-clause-phrase column (Heading, First Detail, Last Control Heading, Last Detail, Footing, Page Limit) and a report-content column. The markdown keeps every word in the right order but destroys the columns: it emits a two-column pipe table whose header cell is 'Logical Top Heading' (zone label fused with the phrase name) and whose body row places 'of Form' in the first column beside '<(first page only) report header lines>', so a reader of the table takes 'of Form' as a row label of report content; 'Logical Page Limit ... Bottom of Form' and 'Physical Bottom of Form the last line that can be printed' likewise fuse zone labels into phrase/content lines. Quotes of both sources check out. The text is present, so no content is missing, but the figure's row/column association (which zone and which PAGE phrase each content line belongs to) is mis-rendered, which is a genuine structural figure defect. Annex D is informative: no normative effect.
verdict.corrected_description: Figure D.6 (informative Annex D) loses its three-column structure in the markdown: zone labels are fused with PAGE phrase names ('Logical Top Heading', 'Logical Page Limit'), and a stray two-column pipe table puts 'of Form' in a row-label cell beside report-content text. All words are present and in order; only the column association is garbled. Structural, no normative effect.
